notes:
SMB inbound from customer support automation stack. Looking to replace parts of their rules engine with LLM. Primary asks: concise ticket summarization, structured JSON outputs for downstream ticket-create/update, and tool-calling to execute triage actions (tag, assign, escalate).

Found via self-serve hosted API sign-up (trial). CS team of ~4 will run pilot. CTO (Maya Singh) is pragmatic—wants low friction POC on public cloud, no private deployment needed right now. Cost sensitivity: medium (focus on cost per ticket). Latency target: sub-500ms for summary on 95th perc (typical ticket length 100-300 tokens). Throughput: ~50 reqs/min during peak.

Model preference: open-models acceptable; want evaluation on quantized variants. Need structured output enforceability (schema + sample outputs) and explicit tool-calling guide for actions into their ticketing API.

Security: require SSO (SAML) for admin console access, SOC2 report for procurement, audit logging for any PII-related actions. Data residency not strict today (US preferred).

Customer quote: 'We want fast, predictable summaries we can feed into automation rules — anything that reduces mean time to resolution by even 10% is a win.'

AE notes: good fit for Hosted API -> low friction. Main risk: budget approval (CFO) + SOC2 docs. Next: send quickstart + pricing, offer 30m technical demo w/ SE, propose 2-week paid POC (cap at $2k) to prove ROI.
